+"""User service."""
+
+from app.db import store
+
+
+def get_user(user_id: int) -> dict | None:
+    return store.get_by_id(user_id)
+
+
+def search_users(query: str) -> list[dict]:
+    # Use standard SQL pattern matching for LIKE, which is case-insensitive for ASCII in SQLite by default
+    return [dict(row) for row in store._conn.execute(
+        "SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name LIKE ? ORDER BY id",
+        (f"%{query}%",)
+    ).fetchall()]

-    return 200, user
+    return 200, user

+
+def handle_search_users(params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
+    q = params.get("q")
+    if not isinstance(q, str) or not q.strip():
+        return 400, {"error": "invalid query"}
+    
+    users_found = users.search_users(q.strip())
+    return 200, {"users": users_found}
+

+from app.api.handlers import handle_search_users
+
+def test_search_users_ok():
+    status, data = handle_search_users({"q": "Ada"})
+    assert status == 200
+    assert data == {"users": [{"id": 1, "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com"}]}
+
+def test_search_users_case_insensitive():
+    status, data = handle_search_users({"q": "ada"})
+    assert status == 200
+    assert len(data["users"]) == 1
+    assert data["users"][0]["name"] == "Ada Lovelace"
+
+def test_search_users_missing_q():
+    status, _ = handle_search_users({})
+    assert status == 400
+
+def test_search_users_blank_q():
+    status, _ = handle_search_users({"q": "   "})
+    assert status == 400
+
+def test_search_users_not_string():
+    status, _ = handle_search_users({"q": 123})
+    assert status == 400
